title: Arlec 2400W Micathermic Heater $37.37 @ Bunnings
body:
Deal: Arlec 2400W Micathermic Heater $37.37 @ Bunnings

[visitorsonlyparking] "Arlec QC" sticker doesn't reassure me even the smallest amount
[shiznit] That sticker is the only thing holding the heater together.
[tonyjzx] heaters are on special because summer is cumming up and i bet you need these damn things when its months on end of 40-50c days my guys
[sushimaster] I hope that's the only thing that's cumming out for now
[tonyjzx] night is still young
also who can do this when its like 12c
[lovrekn] It's not high fashion - it will be just as useful next winter
[kingmoron] Any gas heaters on special ? I can only find expensive ones
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] what makes it Micathermic.
I know about Ceramic fan heater they are more efficient but never heard of Micthermic.
[Herbs] How is a ceramic fan heater more efficient?
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] how? I don't know that's why im asking about Micethermic.
or do you mean how do I know ceramic fan heater is more efficient? because it says so on the heater.
normal old fan heater consumes about 1.5kW on level 1, and 2.4kW on level 2. ceramic fan heater consumes 1kW on level 1, and 2kW max on level 2. it's just more efficient I don't know how but it is. just look it up ceramic is more efficient producing the same heat for some reason.
[MasterScythe] Its very minor. Less is lost to visible light, thats all.
Ceramic is still inferior to IR if you're heating the human in the room.
Ceramic wins if you're heating the rooms air.
Heater science is kinda cool (no pun intended), but the first law of thermodynamics means they're all pretty darn similar.
[Nom] normal old fan heater consumes about 1.5kW on level 1, and 2.4kW on level 2. ceramic fan heater consumes 1kW on level 1, and 2kW max on level 2
Erm, the difference between the 1.5KW fan heater and the 1KW fan heater, is that the second one is only putting 66% as much heat into the room.
1KW of heat is 1KW of heat. If another resistive heater consumes 2.5KW then it's putting 2.5x more heat into the room!
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] @Nom: I don't need the explanation someone who larps as my science teacher.
if you quickly googled you would know the real answer. things are not always as they seems.
"Yes, ceramic fan heaters are more efficient in daily use because their self-regulating plates lower power draw as they warm up, meaning a lower max watt model can still feel stronger and use less electricity than a standard coil fan heater.".
even masterscythe seems to know more than you, they are slightly more efficient. I'm not saying half the power, just slightly more efficient.
as described the new ceramic heater has lower max of 2kW. so consumes 2kWh per hour. and it is equal in heat or even slightly better, but tbf that might because the old fan heater is old.
[Nom] @skibidigrimacmoggr67:
Yes, ceramic fan heaters are more efficient in daily use
The efficiency is exactly the same as any other resistive electric heater.
If you put 1KW in then you get 1KW of heat in your room. Put 2KW in and you get 2KW of heat in your room.
It really is as simple as that.
You can slow down the heat if you put oil in the way, or speed it up with a fan - but either way, the same amount of heat is going into your room.
[richy_o] Don't be fooled by whatever technology they are offering, if it's 2400W then that's 2.4kw per hour every hour it is on. It's like boiling a kettle non stop. Very inefficient.
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] if it's 2400W
oh missed that part. so it's "Micathermic" but still consumes the same amount as a regular fan heater. 😅
[MasterScythe] First law of thermodynamics, sadly.
Elecricity to heat is a near lossless conversion at the end-user level, it can't get notably better unless we discover new thermodynamic science.
[OnlyHans] In this house we obey the laws of thermodynamics!
[Mokr] The benefit of Micathermic is you get the heat near instantly and once you turn it off there's no wasted stored heat like in an oil heater.
[piston3461] How’s the stored heat wasted ? If anything it’s more efficient since it stays warm for a while without being on and using any power
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] there are people who will only believe the math. e.g. 2kWh battery will last you exactly 1 hour powering 2kw.
and then there are people who know things are not what they seems and irl not everything is "exact".
[rd] I have one of these. Only benefit is it heats up quickly. But at 2.4kw you'd better just turn on AC which generate more heat.
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] But at 2.4kw you'd better just turn on AC which generate more heat.
yes use AC if you have it.
[gunslinger] Good deal.
I have a couple like this I run between 1100-1400 each day when it's free power.
[aussieprepper] Just buy a 13/14th gen Intel CPU, great heaters lol.
[Namidairo] Just remember to update your bios before use, otherwise they burn themselves out. (This is not a joke)
